gpu: NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation (1 of 2, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0)
status: COMPLETE for the fovbench half. Runs A and C both landed, so the vggt360 row is readable: A is the method, C is the resolution control, and neither is publishable without the other. The slambench half is results/slambench-023-*.

fov_A.what: the row itself -- five published models re-run BESIDE vggt360 in one command, so the comparison is within a run rather than across two

fov_C.what: the resolution control -- identical to A's vggt360 cell except the nine tangent views are cut from the 518 resize the vanilla models see, instead of from ADT's native 1408 frame
fov_C.command: python -m fovbench.run --adt-root $ADT --n-frames 50 --models vggt360 --views fisheye --protocols radial --workers 1 --vggt360-source view --out eval_out/vggt360-023/fov_C
fov_C.controlled: same split digest 601fcb22767e, same n_frames 300, same input_size 518, same in_cone_frac 0.7551. The ONLY thing that differs between A and C is where the views were cut from, which is what makes the gap a resolution term and not a bundle of them.

n_frames.why: the ticket's own self-check -- 'the vanilla cells must match the #019 headline run, because views and protocols are not in the split digest' -- only works at the frame count the reference used. The published #019 headline is results/fovbench-rectfix-393cab9/partA_6seq: 6 sequences x 50 frames, digest 601fcb22767e. 25 frames reproduces no published digest on this box; the older 25-frame run (fovbench-main-22c108d / 2ab412af0ccc) is a ONE-sequence run from when only 1 of 20 ADT sequences carried all three streams, and there are 6 now.

deviations_from_the_ticket.da3_small_added: costs ~85 s and turns the self-check from three exact-match rows into four. fovbench aligns and scores per model, so adding one cannot perturb the others -- and the self-check below confirms it did not.

workers.why: fovbench deadlocks on this box at dav2_large at any thread count above 1: 498 threads at --workers 8, 754 at --workers 16, every one sleeping in futex_wait, GPU 0%, no frame line ever printed. Not starvation (469 GB RAM free, load 2.3/64 cores) and not the HF Hub (dav2_large alone scores a frame in 6 s, online or HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1). _ordered_map pools rows in split order so serial is bit-identical to threaded, and tests/test_end_to_end.py pins that -- confirmed here by the self-check, which is exact against a reference produced with --workers 16.
workers.cpu_ticket_worth_filing: results/fovbench-rectfix-393cab9 ran the same 300 frames and same models at --workers 16 on 2026-08-14 without hanging, so something under the harness moved in three days.

self_check.what: views and protocols are not in the split digest, so this run carries the same digest as the #019 headline and its vanilla fisheye/radial cells must match it

expected_to_move.why: the reference predates ticket 021, which opened the bf16 autocast VGGTBackbone is written to expect. Its vggt_1b column is fp32. Well inside #021's measured <=0.51% bound.

headline.read_the_bins_not_the_pool: the pooled column hides the entire result. vggt360 and vggt_1b are level on it (0.1198 both, run A) and they are not doing remotely the same thing. AbsRel by incidence bin, real stream, centre (0-10 deg) -> rim (50-55 deg): vggt_1b 0.0957 -> 0.1529 (1.60x), vggt_omega 0.0574 -> 0.1160 (2.02x), da3_large 0.0778 -> 0.1515 (1.95x), da3_small 0.1466 -> 0.2160 (1.47x), dav2_large 0.1379 -> 0.1394 (1.01x), vggt360 0.1240 -> 0.1295 (1.04x). vggt360 is WORSE at the centre than the VGGT-1B it wraps and BETTER at the rim, crossing over around 40 deg.

resolution_control.why_it_exists: run A is not equal-pixel and it leans this row's way: the nine tangent views are cut from ADT's native 1408 frame (0.62x DOWN to 518) while the vanilla models see a 518 resize, from which the same views would be 1.69x UP. `native` says what the method is worth; `view` says what it is worth on the pixels everyone else got.
resolution_control.what_it_does_NOT_change: the shape, which is the claim. Centre -> rim on equal pixels is 0.1330 -> 0.1417 = 1.07x (native 1.04x), against vggt_1b's 1.60x. The crossover against vggt_1b stays at ~40 deg in both: at 40-50 deg vggt360 0.1175 beats vggt_1b 0.1258, at 30-40 deg it does not (0.1234 vs 0.1076). So the resolution term moves the LEVEL and not the SHAPE, and the flatness across the field is not a resolution artefact.
resolution_control.what_it_DOES_change: the pooled ranking, and this has to be said next to the number. On equal pixels vggt360's pooled real AbsRel is 0.12764, which is BEHIND the vggt_1b it wraps (0.11983) rather than level with it. Quoting run A's pooled column alone overstates this row.
resolution_control.synthetic_is_the_weaker_case: the synthetic stream loses more to equal pixels (+14.86%) and its rim bin degrades further (1.08x native -> 1.20x view), so the flatness claim is strongest on the real stream and should be stated there.

log_lines_the_tables_cannot_carry.constant_fill: PASS, by silence. fovbench/models.py:_report_holes prints 'N% of the imaged cone had no view covering it and was filled with a constant' only when the worst-seen fraction exceeds 1%. It never printed across all 300 frames of either run, so the ring tiled its cone within 1% throughout -- which is what the ticket predicted ('expect well under 1%'). Absence of the line IS the result here; do not read it as the diagnostic not running.
log_lines_the_tables_cannot_carry.ring_coverage: 'lens cone 55.11 deg | layout reaches 56.0 deg (102%) | ring reaches the rim' -- the 60 deg layout over-covers the lens, so no --vggt360-ring-tilt rescue was needed and no rim bin is short of geometry. fov_C's report independently confirms the fisheye view is whole to 54.6 deg with the 50-55 bin at 98% azimuth coverage, so the rim bin is a real ring and not corner wedges.
